metaDescription: Compare Kaş and Kalkan for diving, boutique stays, Kekova Sunken City boats or kayaks, airport transfers from DLM/AYT, and the Kaş–Meis ferry.
quickAnswer: Kaş suits travelers who want walkable streets, reef and wreck diving, and small boutique hotels, while Kalkan favors hillside private villas and rooftop dining. Both sit 20–30 minutes apart along the D400 highway, roughly 2 hours 15 minutes to 3 hours from Dalaman or Antalya airports, with easy access to Kekova Sunken City and the Kaş–Meis ferry.

body.text: What is the difference in vibe between Kaş and Kalkan?

Kaş feels like a lived-in Mediterranean port town with narrow cobbled lanes, independent dive centers, casual meyhanes, and small sea-facing boutique stays on the Çukurbağ Peninsula. Kalkan, 27 kilometers west, is steeper and quieter by day, built around hillside infinity-pool villas, beach platforms, and white-tablecloth rooftop restaurants overlooking a sheltered bay.

Neither town has sandy beaches in the center; swimming happens off stone platforms, timber decks, and pebble coves like Küçük Çakıl or Kaputaş. Kaş draws divers, Lycian Way hikers, and travelers who stroll to coffee shops and casual seafood spots. Kalkan caters to families and villa groups who spend afternoons poolside before Old Town terrace dinners.

How do you visit the Kekova Sunken City by private boat or kayak?

You reach the Kekova Sunken City either by boarding a private wooden boat from Kaş or Üçağız harbor, or by joining a guided sea-kayak paddle launching from Üçağız. Because the underwater Lycian ruins of Dolchiste hold first-degree archaeological protection, swimming, snorkeling, and diving directly over the sunken walls are strictly prohibited; viewing happens from the water's surface.

As documented by [GoTürkiye](https://goturkiye.com/culturaljourneys/kayaking), the northern flank of Kekova Island holds stone staircases, quays, and foundations that slipped below sea level after ancient earthquakes. The zone has been a Specially Protected Environmental Area since 1990, and [local Kaş conservation guidance](https://ghostofkas.com/guides/why-you-cant-swim-over-the-sunken-city/) confirms that only guided kayaks may glide quietly over the shallowest ruins without stopping or touching stone, while motorboats cruise slowly along the outer line.
Choosing between boat and kayak comes down to pace and heat:

items: Private boat from Üçağız: Skips the 90-minute open-water run from Kaş, leaving extra time to swim in [Tersane, Aquarium, and İnönü bays](https://kaspeninsulagardens.com/discover-kekova-sunken-city-your-ultimate-guide-to-turkeys-underwater-lycian-wonder-from-kas/) and climb Simena Castle.
Guided sea kayaking from Üçağız: Best in April–June or September–October on glassy morning water, paddling 6–8 kilometers past sunken walls and Simena's sarcophagi.
Scuba diving in Kaş: Since diving is banned at Kekova, dive Kaş's reefs, canyon walls, and wrecks 10–25 minutes offshore.

body.text: How far is Kaş from Dalaman and Antalya airports?

Dalaman Airport (DLM) is closer to both Kalkan and Kaş, sitting 150–160 kilometers northwest for a 2.5-hour drive along the D400 via Fethiye and Kalkan. Antalya Airport (AYT) lies 185–195 kilometers east, taking 2.5 to 3.5 hours along the winding coastal road via Kemer, Finike, and Demre.

Per [2026 transfer benchmarks](https://www.joytransfer.com/en/blog/how-far-is-kas-from-dalaman-airport-2026-transfer-prices) and [D400 driving guides](https://kas-rent-a-car.com/antalya-airport-to-kas/), Dalaman offers faster, smoother driving (note the Göcek Tunnel toll), while Antalya wins on year-round flight frequency. For late-night arrivals, pre-book a private driver rather than tackling the coastal curves tired. Pairing Kaş with a yacht week? See our [Göcek sailing](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/gocek-turkey-sailing) and [2026 gulet charter](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/gulet-charter-turkey-2026) guides.
Can you take a day ferry from Kaş to Kastellorizo (Meis)?

Yes. Direct passenger ferries connect Kaş harbor to Greece's Kastellorizo (Meis) in 7 to 20 minutes across a 6-kilometer strait. Bring a valid passport meeting Schengen entry rules—an EU/visa-exempt passport or valid Schengen visa—and check in at Kaş port one hour before departure.

[Meis Ferry Lines, Meis Express](https://www.ferryhopper.com/en/ferries/turkey/kas), and [Ertürk Lines](https://www.erturk.com.tr/en/kas-meis-timetable) run morning crossings (09:30–10:00) returning around 16:00, with reduced off-season schedules. Per [Ferryhopper](https://www.ferryhopper.com/en/ferry-routes/direct/kas-kastellorizo) and [crossing notes](https://www.getyourguide.com/kas-l1382/5-hour-ferry-from-kas-to-kastellorizo-t17825/), carry small cash for harbor taxes. On arrival, take a water taxi to the Blue Grotto before noon, then linger over lunch on the waterfront.

faq.q: Is Kaş or Kalkan better if I do not rent a car?
faq.a: Kaş is much easier without a car because the town center, harbor, dive boats, and minibuses sit within walking distance. Kalkan's hillside villas routinely require taxis back from dinner.

faq.q: Can you swim or snorkel over the Kekova Sunken City?
faq.a: No. Swimming, snorkeling, and scuba diving are prohibited directly over the sunken ruins of Dolchiste under first-degree archaeological protection. Boat and kayak trips include swim stops in permitted nearby bays such as Tersane Bay and Aquarium Bay.

faq.q: Which airport is better for Kalkan: Dalaman or Antalya?
faq.a: Dalaman Airport (DLM) is much closer to Kalkan—roughly 125 kilometers or 1 hour 45 minutes by road—compared with roughly 3 hours or more from Antalya Airport (AYT). Choose Antalya only if Dalaman lacks flights on your travel dates.

faq.q: Do I need to book the Kaş to Kastellorizo ferry in advance?
faq.a: Yes, especially from June through September. Ferry offices submit passenger manifest and passport details to Turkish and Greek border authorities ahead of sailing, so booking at least 24 to 48 hours early avoids sold-out crossings.

faq.q: How many days should I spend in Kaş and Kalkan?
faq.a: Three to four nights cover one day for Kekova by boat or kayak, one day for diving or Kastellorizo, and one day for Patara, Xanthos, and Saklıkent.

faq.q: Is Kaş good for beginner scuba divers?
faq.a: Yes. Kaş has sheltered shallow bays with clear Mediterranean visibility, reputable dive schools, and easy training sites alongside deeper walls and wrecks for certified divers.
